text:
Good evening. Today is Monday, November 9th. First, the news from home.

Story one. Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has urged the Majority and Minority caucuses to build bipartisan consensus on proposed amendments to the 1992 Constitution. Graphic Online reports that Speaker Bagbin warned partisan disagreements could frustrate governance reforms, stressing that constitutional review must be treated as a national undertaking rather than a political contest.

Story two. Graphic Online reports that the former National Chairman of the N D C, Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, has stepped down from the party's national chairmanship contest. A statement issued on his behalf explained that he has chosen to focus on his advisory roles at COCOBOD and to the Vice President.

Story three. The Majority in Parliament has alleged that the previous N P P administration facilitated a service passport racketeering scheme at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Graphic Online reports that the Majority claims the former government recruited an individual near the end of its tenure to continue the irregular issuance of service passports dating back to 2023.

Story four. Three News reports that the Office of the Special Prosecutor is examining alleged corruption and financial discrepancies involving forty-nine point seven million Ghana cedis spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa.

Now, around the world.

Story five. The B B C, Africanews, and Al Jazeera report that at least thirty-nine people have died after a migrant boat bound for Europe sank off the coast of Senegal. Human rights advocates in Senegal are calling for urgent government action to address the dangerous Atlantic crossings to Spain's Canary Islands.

Story six. According to the B B C and Africanews, nine Zimbabwean nationals have been apprehended in South Africa while allegedly attempting to travel to Ukraine to fight for Russian forces. Ukrainian officials report that hundreds of individuals from across Africa have been recruited into the war.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
